entries.context: Post-Wave2 · algebra · associative ring with a multiplicative identity
entries.definition: A unital ring is an associative ring (R,+,·,0) equipped with an element 1_R such that 1_R·r=r=r·1_R for every r∈R. Multiplication is not required to be commutative. The zero ring, where 0=1_R, is included unless a nonzero-ring convention is stated.
entries.research_status: post-Wave2 assistant-reviewed draft; not formally certified
assumptions: Associativity is assumed for the underlying ring.
The zero ring is not excluded by this definition.

entries.definition: For unital rings R and S, a unital ring homomorphism f:R→S is an additive map satisfying f(ab)=f(a)f(b) for all a,b∈R and f(1_R)=1_S. In particular f preserves 0. Some authors include preservation of 1 in the unqualified term 'ring homomorphism'; others do not.
entries.research_status: post-Wave2 assistant-reviewed draft; not formally certified
assumptions: Both source and target have designated multiplicative identities.
Explicit identity preservation distinguishes this convention from a nonunital homomorphism.

entries.context: Post-Wave2 · category theory · smallness of morphism collections
entries.definition: A category C is locally small if, for every ordered pair of objects X,Y of C, the collection Hom_C(X,Y) of morphisms from X to Y is a set rather than a proper class (relative to the chosen foundational universe). Its collection of objects need not be a set. Every small category is locally small, but the converse need not hold.
entries.research_status: post-Wave2 assistant-reviewed draft; not formally certified
assumptions: The set-versus-proper-class distinction is interpreted relative to a fixed foundational universe.

entries.context: Post-Wave2 · commutative algebra · nonnegative integer grading (Stacks convention)
entries.definition: A nonnegatively graded (commutative, unital) ring S is a commutative unital ring together with an additive-group direct-sum decomposition S=⊕_{d≥0} S_d such that S_d·S_e⊆S_{d+e} for all d,e≥0. Every element of S is a finite sum of homogeneous elements. This is a nonnegative-integer grading; more general grading groups are separate conventions.
entries.research_status: post-Wave2 assistant-reviewed draft; not formally certified
assumptions: Commutative, unital-ring convention as in the cited Stacks Project section.
The grading is indexed by the nonnegative integers, not all integers or an arbitrary group.
